entities.name: Job lifecycle
entities.description: Ordered state machine. raised → scheduled → dispatched → in_progress → completed → invoiced, with cancelled reachable from any state before completed. Dispatcher drives the first three transitions; technician drives in_progress and completed; invoiced is a billing run, not a human action. A completed job may be REOPENED back to in_progress by a dispatcher only, with a recorded reason and actor; if the job was already invoiced, its invoice must be voided first. Reopening is distinct from cancelling — a completed job still cannot be cancelled.

sources.quote: in_progress — the technician starts it, on site. completed — the technician closes it, with notes.
The transitions are ordered. A job does not skip from raised to in_progress.
A dispatcher can move a completed job back to in_progress with a recorded reason and actor.

entities.name: Assign a technician to a job
entities.description: Dispatcher selects a technician and a time window; the system rejects the assignment if it overlaps an existing assignment for that technician; on success the job becomes scheduled. Multi-step write: create the assignment and advance the job status.

sources.quote: An assignment that overlaps an existing assignment for that technician must be rejected, not warned about.

entities.name: Generate an invoice from a completed job
entities.description: A completed job produces an invoice with lines and a total, and the job moves to invoiced. Multi-step write across two collections.

sources.quote: A completed job produces an invoice record with line items and a total.

entities.name: A technician cannot be double-booked
entities.description: No two ACTIVE assignments may share (technician, date, slot). Enforced by a unique partial index on active assignments, so concurrency is resolved by the database: the second concurrent write fails on the duplicate key and the service translates that into 409. A superseded assignment must NOT block the slot, which is why the index is partial rather than plain.

sources.quote: a technician cannot be double-booked
Two dispatchers assigning the same technician to overlapping slots at the same moment must not both succeed.
Double-booking becomes a unique index on (technician, date, slot) ... The service catches that and returns 409.

entities.enforcement: unique partial index on (technician, date, slot) where status = 'active'

openQuestions.question: What is a time slot — a fixed grid (hourly, or morning/afternoon), or an arbitrary start and end datetime chosen per job?
openQuestions.why: Decides Assignment's fields and how the overlap check is expressed. A fixed grid makes double-booking a unique index on (technician, slot); arbitrary windows make it a range-overlap query that a unique index cannot enforce, which changes the atomicity strategy for con-no-double-booking.
openQuestions.answer: Fixed grid. An assignment is (technician, date, slot) with slot in {morning, afternoon, evening}. A job occupies exactly one slot. No-double-booking is enforced by a unique partial index on active assignments; the duplicate-key failure becomes a 409.

openQuestions.question: Can a dispatched or in-progress job be reassigned to a different technician, and what happens to the original assignment — replaced, or kept as history?
openQuestions.why: Decides whether Job↔Assignment is 1:1 or 1:N with one active. Changes the schema, the overlap check and at least two stories.
openQuestions.answer: Yes, with history. Job↔Assignment is 1:N with exactly one active assignment; reassigning marks the old one superseded and creates a new active one. Superseded assignments do not block a slot.

openQuestions.question: Does completing a job require anything beyond notes — a photo, a customer signature, parts used, time on site?
openQuestions.why: Each addition is a required field and an acceptance criterion. Photos additionally mean file upload, which brings its own OWASP surface (size limits, content-type validation, storage location).

openQuestions.question: A completed job cannot be cancelled (3.2). What happens when a completed or invoiced job turns out to be wrong?
openQuestions.why: There is currently no correction path in the stated lifecycle. Without one, the first real mistake has no in-system remedy and someone edits the database by hand.
openQuestions.answer: A dispatcher (not a technician) may reopen a completed job back to in_progress, recording a reason and actor. If the job was invoiced, its invoice is voided first. Cancelling a completed job remains forbidden.

openQuestions.question: Where do invoice line prices come from — typed by the dispatcher, a rate card, or derived from time on site and parts used?
openQuestions.why: Every attribute of InvoiceLine is currently 'implied'. A rate card is an entity nobody has mentioned; deriving from time on site depends on q-completion-requirements.

openQuestions.question: Can a customer be deleted while they have open jobs, and can a job exist without a customer?
openQuestions.why: Decides required-ness and the delete strategy (block, cascade, or soft-delete). Getting it wrong orphans jobs.

openQuestions.question: How is a technician deactivated when they leave, and what happens to their future assignments?
openQuestions.why: The 'active' attribute on Technician is currently 'assumed' — nobody stated it. Deletion would orphan assignment history, so deactivation is likely, but that must be confirmed, and the unassignment of future work is a real workflow nobody has described.

openQuestions.question: Must a cancellation carry a reason, and who is allowed to cancel — dispatcher only, or the technician too?
openQuestions.why: The 'cancelledReason' attribute is 'assumed' and section 3.3 names an owner for every transition except cancellation.

openQuestions.question: What retention period and data residency apply to customer addresses and technician scheduling data?
openQuestions.why: Both are personal data. GDPR applicability is unresolved in PROFILE.md, and retention must be decided in /design-schema rather than after launch.

openQuestions.question: Can a technician have more than one job in the same slot if the dispatcher explicitly overrides, or is the slot hard-limited to one job always?
openQuestions.why: Decides whether the unique index is the whole rule or needs an override path. An override would mean the index cannot be the enforcement mechanism, which reverses the q-slot-shape decision.

openQuestions.question: Who may void an invoice, must voiding carry a reason, and can a paid invoice be voided?
openQuestions.why: Reopening an invoiced job voids its invoice (8.3), but nobody has said who else may void, whether a reason is required, or what happens to an invoice already marked paid. Voiding a paid invoice is a money-affecting action with no stated owner.

openQuestions.question: After a reopened job is completed again, does it generate a new invoice automatically, and what links it to the voided one?
openQuestions.why: The invoice generation process assumes a completed job has no prior invoice. Without an answer, a re-completed job either silently skips invoicing or creates an unlinked duplicate.
